top_story.headline: Army put armed guards in Erbil, Iraq, to work on September 10 and justified skipping competition on October 8
top_story.dek: The task order supports U.S. Army Central and the Operation Inherent Resolve task force, and its dollar value is redacted.
paragraphs: The Department of the Army's contracting command at Rock Island issued a notice to proceed on September 10, 2026 to GardaWorld Federal Services for armed guard services near Erbil International Airport, then awarded the work as an undefinitized task order under the Global Protective Services contract. The justification for an exception to fair opportunity, a post-award document, is dated October 8, 2026.

The Army says about 20 days remained to mobilize and obtain the approvals needed for armed performance, and chose GardaWorld as the vendor most immediately able to perform based on responses to a request for information. The requiring activity is U.S. Army Central and the Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve. The value is redacted in the public document.

Also in today's justifications: a $152.8 million ceiling increase for CACI at the General Services Administration, and a bridge contract for Air Force fuel-system maintenance while a protest is pending at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

sections.headline: Army skipped competition for armed guards in Erbil, Iraq, and wrote the justification after the work started
paragraphs: 52 new sole-source justifications and 922 new solicitations were posted October 8–9, 2026; none had been covered in an earlier edition, and 97 solicitation amendments to items already flagged are left out. The five must-read items are below; every other justification is linked at the bottom.

blocks.title: Army hires GardaWorld to guard Erbil, Iraq, and paperwork on skipping competition came after work began
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Army's contracting office at Rock Island issued a notice to proceed on September 10, 2026 for armed guard services near Erbil International Airport, supporting U.S. Army Central and the Combined Joint Task Force for Operation Inherent Resolve, and awarded it as an undefinitized task order. The justification for skipping competition among existing contract holders is dated October 8, 2026, so it was written after the award. The Army says about 20 days were left to mobilize armed guards, and picked GardaWorld as the vendor most immediately able to perform based on responses to a request for information.

blocks.title: Homeland Security extends court-ordered family reunification help to the International Organization for Migration, after the old contract ran out
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: This is the follow-on to a 2021 sole-source contract set up to comply with a court order in the Miss L. v. Immigration and Customs Enforcement class action, which required the government to return separated families to the United States. The prior contract's options ran through September 12, 2026. The justification says the Secretary of Homeland Security decided in late fiscal year 2025 to move administration from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, and that the agency lacked the roughly 120 days needed to compete the work, citing the risk of violating the settlement if services lapsed.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers buys a sole-source bridge to keep Air Force fuel-system maintenance going while a protest is pending
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Army, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Huntsville Engineering and Support Center
blocks.text: The justification covers up to 336 days of preventive and corrective maintenance and emergency repair for the North Atlantic Division–Air Force fuels program, starting September 29, 2026, the day after the current task order expires, with a 66-day base and three 90-day options. The Corps says the bridge is needed because protest litigation over the follow-on contract is still active and the successor contractor cannot begin transition until a notice to proceed is issued. The requiring activity is the Defense Logistics Agency's energy office.

blocks.title: General Services Administration lifts a task order ceiling by $152.8 million for CACI without a new competition
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The agency's Federal Systems Integration and Management Center intends to raise the ceiling on a task order for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities and threat analysis support for an Army command-and-control center. It calls the increase a logical follow-on to an existing competed order, with scope unchanged but mission demand above estimates. The document says earlier internal funding realignments are exhausted, making a ceiling increase the only way to sustain operations.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement buys 366 reserved parking spaces for its Washington headquarters, citing the return-to-office order
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The sole-source buy is for 366 spaces in the Potomac Center South underground garage at 550 12th Street SW in Washington, D.C. The agency says the spaces provide overflow capacity because of a surge in reasonable-accommodation requests and other authorized parking under the Return to In-Person Work executive order, and that the garage is the only facility with a secure connection to its headquarters and security modifications suited to an elevated threat environment that includes frequent protests.

items: U.S. Department of Homeland Security — Thales fingerprint-matching software licensing and maintenance for the biometric systems IDENT and HART; vendor Thales DIS USA Inc.; value redacted; the agency says the government and third parties cannot get the source code and interfaces (SSJ_FY26_0190).

Department of the Navy — third bridge for custodial services at Naval District Washington, up to 12 months after two Government Accountability Office protests delayed the replacement award; vendor NJS Joint Venture, LLC; value redacted (N40080-26-JA-011).

Department of the Air Force — eight tactical communication kits built around SpaceX Starshield terminals for aeromedical evacuation, brand name only; vendor NexTech Solutions with Space Exploration Technologies Corp. terminals; value redacted (AECommsKitsBNOJA2026).
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — Hootsuite social media platform and Talkwalker visual recognition for public affairs; vendor Hootsuite Inc.; value redacted (JA-26-0292).

Washington Headquarters Services — bridge of support services for a Department of Defense ManTech program, two-month base plus four one-month options; vendor PM2 Strategies; value redacted (HQ003426PE158).

U.S. Coast Guard — request for proposals for the Homeland Security Cutter – Light Icebreaker, an indefinite-delivery contract for design and production of a new vessel class, two-phase down-select (70Z02326R93280004).

Solicitations not listed (about 824): Defense Logistics Agency, 336, Department of the Navy, 194, Department of Veterans Affairs, 73, Department of the Army, 65, Department of the Air Force, 29, Department of Agriculture, 25, Department of the Interior, 14, National Aeronautics and Space Administration, 12; all other agencies, 76. The 922 new solicitations also include 97 amendments to solicitations already flagged in earlier editions (new deadlines or question-and-answer updates), which are omitted. All 922 solicitations in the window were fetched; no quota was hit.

sections.headline: No new contract awards of $2 million or more; four under-$2 million awards stand out
paragraphs: No new awards of $2 million or more appeared in the September 14–October 9, 2026 sweep. Among 45 new awards between $100,000 and $2 million from October 6–9, four are worth a line each; none involves the White House or the Executive Office of the President.

items: Deloitte Consulting LLP — $1,199,958, National Aeronautics and Space Administration: program support covering systems engineering, integration, risk and certification expertise for lunar landing missions at Marshall Space Flight Center (award).

Fasone Construction, Inc. — $1,147,809, General Services Administration: task order for "court hardening" at the Richard H. Chambers Courthouse in Pasadena, California, a security upgrade to a federal courthouse (award).
Procare Ambulance of Maryland, Inc. — $1,252,145, Department of Veterans Affairs: first ordering period of ambulance services for the Washington, D.C. VA Medical Center (award).

Hirt Electric, LLC — $585,400, Department of Veterans Affairs: chiller replacement at the Huntington VA Medical Center, with a modification adding the new federal clause on diversity, equity and inclusion discrimination (FAR 52.222-90) — routine boilerplate rather than a dispute (award).

blocks.text: 45 new awards under $2 million were screened; all 4 flagged are listed above and 41 are routine, led by 22 from the Department of Veterans Affairs and 5 from the General Services Administration. One award worth $1.2 million cites Executive Order 14398 in its description.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files approved in this window
paragraphs: The federal apportionment process — in which the Office of Management and Budget releases appropriated funds to agencies in quarterly tranches — produced no new filings between October 4–9, 2026. Both OpenOMB.org and the official apportionment tracking system remained accessible with no new flagged items or spend-plan modifications of note.
